findings.title: Shard splitting interpolates every query twice
findings.body:
runSplitQuery now always maps targets through datasource.applyTemplateVariables before grouping and execution. runShardSplitQuery does the same (shardQuerySplitting.ts:52) and then, for every shard group, calls runSplitQuery (shardQuerySplitting.ts:163) with targets that are already interpolated and rewritten by interpolateShardingSelector. Substitution therefore runs twice on every shard-split query. The updated shard test locks this in by expecting applyTemplateVariables 5 times for one target (once up front, once per group) and stubs an idempotent string replace, so it never fails.

applyTemplateVariables is not idempotent: it both expands variables and injects request.filters into the LogQL. The second call sees the already substituted text plus the __stream_shard__ selector. Ad hoc filters are applied again onto a selector that was not the input the injector first rewrote, so matchers are duplicated and can be attached in the wrong place, producing invalid LogQL or a selector that no longer matches the shard values fetched on the first pass. Template replacement also does not rescan substituted values within one pass, so a label or line-filter value such as team-$env is left intact the first time and then expanded on the second pass if env is a dashboard variable. The same query with shard splitting off is interpolated only once, so shard splitting silently returns different streams. Interpolate once: keep a single applyTemplateVariables step for shard grouping, and skip it inside runSplitQuery when the caller has already prepared the targets.

findings.title: Shard path no longer pre-expands $__range, so those queries are not time-split
findings.body:
runShardSplitQuery used to call interpolateVariablesInQueries(request.targets, request.scopedVars), which substitutes every scoped variable, including $__range, $__range_s, and $__range_ms, against the original request range. It now calls applyTemplateVariables, which deliberately strips __range, __range_s, __range_ms, __interval, and __interval_ms out of scoped vars so those macros stay in the expression for the backend.

The still-macro expressions are passed into runSplitQuery. querySupportsSplitting (querySplitting.ts:282-288) refuses to time-split any expression that still contains $__range, because the backend would otherwise interpolate it with the chunk time range. Previously the macro was already a constant full-range duration, the guard did not match, and the query was still chunked with a correct lookback. After this change, a shard-split metric query such as count_over_time({job="x"}[$__range]) over a multi-day dashboard range is sent as one unsplit request. The range value stays correct, but queries that previously completed via chunking can now hit Loki's max query duration or time out. $__interval / $__interval_ms are also no longer baked in from the original scoped vars, so the backend expands them per sub-request instead of using the dashboard interval. The new tests stub templateSrv.replace with a blind replace of $__auto and $step, so they never observe this. Expand range macros against the original scoped vars before the splitting decision (while still using applyTemplateVariables for step, legend, and ad hoc filters), or explicitly accept the no-split behavior and test it.

findings.title: Expressions that interpolate to empty are no longer dropped before sharding
findings.body: The previous shard entry point interpolated first and then dropped targets with a falsy expr. The new code filters on query.expr and !query.hide and only then calls applyTemplateVariables, with no second filter. A target whose expression is only a template variable that resolves to an empty string (a common optional dashboard variable) used to be removed and not executed. It is now passed into splitQueriesByStreamShard and groupTargetsByQueryType, which calls getSelectorForShardValues on that empty expression and languageProvider.fetchLabelValues for __stream_shard__. runSplitQuery later drops empty expressions, so the target is not queried, but the label lookup still runs and failures are only logged. If selector extraction throws, groupTargetsByQueryType rejects and the .then at shardQuerySplitting.ts:213 has no .catch, so the query observable never emits or completes and the panel hangs. Filter again after applyTemplateVariables, as the old interpolate-then-filter order did.
